title: A Volunteer’s Journal
label: 問5
passageHtml:
From Noah’s Volunteer Journal

When I signed up to help at the city animal shelter, I imagined playing with dogs. On my first morning, however, Ms. Chen handed me a bucket and showed me how to clean the cages. I was disappointed, but I tried to work quickly.

Later, I noticed a small dog named Pepper refusing to eat. Ms. Chen explained that Pepper became nervous around new people. Instead of touching her, I sat quietly outside the cage and read my history notes aloud. After several visits, Pepper began eating while I was there.

On my final day, a family came to meet Pepper. She stayed behind me at first, but then slowly walked toward the youngest child. Seeing that, I understood that the cleaning and quiet hours had mattered. The work was not what I had expected, but it had taught me to pay attention rather than simply try to be useful in the way I preferred.

questions.question: What did Noah expect to do at the shelter?
questions.reason_ja: 最初の期待を直接問う問題です。

questions.question: Why did Noah read aloud near Pepper?
options: To let her become used to him without pressure
questions.answer: To let her become used to him without pressure
questions.evidence: Instead of touching her, I sat quietly ... and read.
questions.reason_ja: 触れずに静かに存在することで、犬の緊張を和らげようとしました。

questions.question: What change shows Pepper trusted Noah more?
options: She ate while he was there
questions.answer: She ate while he was there
questions.evidence: After several visits, Pepper began eating while I was there.
questions.reason_ja: 食べるようになったことが安心感の変化を示します。

questions.question: What lesson did Noah learn?
options: Useful work must always be enjoyable
Helping requires noticing what is actually needed
Volunteers should choose only easy tasks
questions.answer: Helping requires noticing what is actually needed
questions.evidence: it had taught me to pay attention rather than simply try to be useful in the way I preferred.
questions.reason_ja: 自分のやりたい支援ではなく、相手に必要な支援を見極めることを学びました。
